draft.title: Consumer guarantees
card: Australian Consumer Law gives buyers consumer guarantees. These are rules that apply automatically when you buy a product from a business.
A product must be safe to use. It must also work as the seller or the packaging described it.
A product must last a reasonable time. What is reasonable depends on the product and its price.
If a product fails a guarantee, you can ask the business for a repair, a replacement or a refund.
draft.remember: If a product is unsafe, not as described or breaks too soon, you can ask for a fix.

a.q: Which situation shows a product that fails a consumer guarantee?
opts: A new kettle is sold as working but will not heat water
A shopper decides she no longer likes her new jumper
A shopper finds the same shoes cheaper at another shop
A buyer forgets to use a toy for a month after buying it
a.why: The kettle does not work as described, so it fails a guarantee. Disliking a jumper is a change of mind, not a fault in the product.
a.clue: Look for a fault in the product, not a change in the buyer's mind.

b.q: Liam buys a new pair of headphones in Hobart. The box says they work with any phone, but they will not connect to his phone. What can he ask the shop to do?
opts: Repair or replace them, or give a refund
Give a refund only if he has changed his mind
Lower the price of other items he buys later
Nothing, because the headphones have been opened
b.why: The headphones do not work as described on the box, so they fail a guarantee. Liam can ask for a repair, replacement or refund. Opening a faulty product does not take away that right.
b.clue: Compare what the box promised with what the headphones did.

a.best: A new kettle is sold as working but will not heat water

b.best: Repair or replace them, or give a refund

problems.detail: 'You can ask for a fix' could be read as a repair only. The card says the buyer can ask for a repair, a replacement or a refund.

check.summary: The facts and both questions are sound. The remember line's 'ask for a fix' is narrower than the card's repair, replacement or refund, and should name all three.
